title: Groundwater and Soil Moisture Conditions from GRACE and GRACE-FO Data Assimilation, global 0.25° weekly (GRACE-DA-DM GL V3.0)
description: Weekly global drought indicators from NASA Goddard: groundwater, root-zone soil moisture and surface soil moisture expressed as percentiles, i.e. the probability of occurrence of the current wetness within the 1948–2014 period of record. The indicators are derived from the GRACE/GRACE-FO-assimilating Catchment model simulation (GLDAS_CLSM025_DA1_D) at 0.25°, are daily values provided for one day (Monday) per week, and run from February 2003 to present with a 3–6 month latency in this final archive.
purpose: Provides ready-to-use groundwater and soil-moisture drought percentiles that can be summarised over Algerian wilayas to describe hydrological and agricultural drought, complementing precipitation-based indices such as SPI and SPEI.

spatial_extent.description: Global from 60° S to 90° N on a 0.25° grid (600 latitude × 1440 longitude cells); Algeria is fully inside the domain. Users subset the global weekly files.

temporal_extent.frequency: weekly (daily values for one day, Monday, per week)
temporal_extent.description: 3 February 2003 to present. The latest granule in CMR on 2026-11-22 was dated 28 September 2026 (1,235 granules). This GES DISC archive is the final version produced after GRACE-FO data are available (3–6 month latency); an operational version with 2–9 day latency is published on the project website.

format: NetCDF-4 (.nc4, one global file per week, about 2 MB)
processing: Percentiles are computed from the GLDAS_CLSM025_DA1_D Catchment (CLSM-F2.5, LIS) simulation forced by ECMWF meteorology and assimilating CSR RL06 GRACE/GRACE-FO mascons, against a 1948–2014 period of record and with a 7-day moving-window climatology (README). The global simulation is restarted from the last available GRACE month and extended to the present each week; TWS anomalies use a 2004–2018 baseline.
validation: Not quantified in the README; Li et al. (2019) discuss the global data assimilation and drought indicators.
limitations: Percentiles are model-derived drought indicators, not measurements; they inherit errors of the ECMWF forcing, the Catchment model parameters and the coarse GRACE constraint.
The README warns that different forcing datasets and data assimilation can create discontinuities; this global product differs from the U.S. GRACE-DA-DM V4.0 product.
Percentile reference period 1948–2014 (from the long model record), while the assimilated record starts in 2003.
Downloads require a free NASA Earthdata Login.

algeria_notes: The percentiles can be averaged over wilayas to compare groundwater and soil-moisture drought with SPI/SPEI. In the Sahara, where soil moisture is near zero and storage changes are dominated by aquifer abstraction, percentile values should be interpreted with great caution.
